title: tshark: Add new long option --hexdump <hexoption>
description:
The legacy tshark -x output generally requires some amount of
routine post-processing before it can be used by text2pcap to
reliably produce a verbatim copy of each of the original capture
file's frames.

There are two issues with directly using tshark's legacy -x
output as input to text2pcap.

Issue 1: Extraneous malformed frames

When tshark is run with the -x option, at least one hexdump block
will be generated for each frame. Because of packet dissection a
frame may have multiple data sources assigned to it.

If a frame has multiple data sources, secondary labeled hexdump
blocks will be generated for that frame. The primary hexdump block
will start with the header label "Frame (N bytes):" where "N" is
the integer number of bytes for the first hexdump block followed
by one or more additional labeled hexdump blocks; one for each of
the secondary data sources. Examples of some of the additional
labels used for secondary data sources include "Bitstring tvb",
"Reassembled TCP", "De-chunked entity body", and others.

When these secondary data source hexdump blocks are presented to
text2pcap, each will be processed as if it actually represents
frame data resulting in extraneous malformed frames in the newly
generated capture file.

The new tshark `--hexdump frames` option will suppress generation
of the hex blocks for the secondary data sources.

Issue 2: Extraneous bytes at the end of some frames

The hexdump blocks generated by tshark's legacy -x output is
formatted in such a way that text2pcap can not always reliably
determine the end of the hexdata section and start of the ASCII
dump text for the last record of each block.

In these cases text2pcap will incorrectly consume data from the
ASCII dump text as hexdata. Any ASCII dump text consumed as
hexdata results in extraneous bytes appended to the end of the
current frame.

The new tshark `--hexdump delimit` or `--hexdump noascii` options
can be used to unambiguously delimit the ASCII dump text or
exclude the ASCII dump text completely for each hex block.

Fixes #14639

notes.body: That isn't guaranteed to remain true forever; it requires reworking of libwireshark and the way it's used to write packets, but that's necessary for a lot of other reasons, and it's one of the things on my plate.
That looks like a separate bug fix; is it?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1784/diffs?diff_id=138086308&start_sha=31cc0c34f69cbc851f9206adf1da9c88cb5edcd0#8936bc80fd9b75c767080e48a0056ac69001cdd6_1421_1421)

Sigh. In amending the original patch via the web UI to create the version 2 diff, the commit message pasted into the UI ended up with whitespace issues resulting in failed pipeline. What's the best way to resolve this?

added 1 commit
  • 0b5cdda8 - tshark: Add new long option --hexdump <hexoption>
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1784/diffs?diff_id=138086308&start_sha=31cc0c34f69cbc851f9206adf1da9c88cb5edcd0)

> What's the best way to resolve this?

Nuke it from orbit, it's the only way to be sure. :-)

I have *no* idea why it's complaining about the *removal* of trailing extra spaces; that just seems like a completely silly thing to complain about.

I'd save your work (changes and commit message), close this pull request, delete any branch you have for it in your GitLab repository, and either uncommit it from your local repository (e.g., with `git reset --hard HEAD^`) or start fresh with a new repository.

Then submit the addition of the newline to the message as a separate fix, and then, once that's merged, re-submit all the other work as a separate fix, with a version of the commit message without the trailing spaces.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -908,6 +908,76 @@ B<n> write network address resolution information (pcapng only)
 Cause B<TShark> to print a hex and ASCII dump of the packet data
 after printing the summary and/or details, if either are also being displayed.
 
+=item --hexdump E<lt>hexoptionE<gt>
+
+Cause B<TShark> to print a hex and ASCII dump of the packet data
+with the ability to select which data sources to dump and how to
+format the ASCII dump text.
+
+This option can be used multiple times on the command line where
+E<lt>hexoptionE<gt> is one of B<all>, B<frames>, B<ascii>,
+B<delimit>, B<noascii>, or B<help>.
+
+Example:  tshark ... --hexdump frames --hexdump noascii ...
+
+=over 4
+
+=item B<all>
+
+Enable hexdump, generate hexdump blocks for all data sources associated
+with each frame. Used to negate earlier use of B<--hexdump frames>.
+Legacy B<-x> option displays all data sources by default.
+
+=item B<frames>
+
+Enable hexdump, generate hexdump blocks only for the frame data. Use
+this option to exclude, from hexdump output, any hexdump blocks for
+secondary data sources such as 'Bitstring tvb', 'Reassembled TCP',
+'De-chunked entity body', etc.
+
+=item B<ascii>
+
+Enable hexdump, with undelimited ASCII dump text. Used to negate earlier
+use of B<--hexdump delimit> or B<--hexdump noascii>. Legacy B<-x> option
+displays undelimited ASCII dump text by default.
+
+=item B<delimit>
+
+Enable hexdump with the ASCII dump text delimited with '|' characters.
+This is useful to unambigiously determine the last of the hex byte text
+and start of the ASCII dump text.
+
+=item B<noascii>
+
+Enable hexdump without printing any ASCII dump text.
+
+=item B<help>
+
+Display --hexdump specific help then exit.
+
+=back
+
+The B<--hexdump> option is particularly useful for helping to generate
+output that can be used to generate a pcap or pcapng file from a capture
+file type such as Microsoft NetMon 2.x which tshark and Wireshark can
+read but can not directly do a "Save as" nor export packets from.
+
+Examples:
+
+Generate hexdump output with delimited ASCII dump text and human
+readable timestamps that is directly usable by the text2pcap utility:
+
+  tshark ... --hexdump frames --hexdump delimit \
+      -P -t ad -o gui.column.format:"Time","%t" \
+      | text2pcap -t '%F %T.' - MYNEWPCAP
+
+Generate hexdump output without any ASCII dump text using epoch
+timestamps that is directly usable by the text2pcap utility:
+
+  tshark ... --hexdump frames --hexdump noascii \
+      -P -t e -o gui.column.format:"Time","%t" \
+      | text2pcap -t %s. - MYNEWPCAP
+
 =item -X E<lt>eXtension optionsE<gt>
 
 Specify an option to be passed to a B<TShark> module.  The eXtension option

@@ -80,7 +80,29 @@ WS_DLL_PUBLIC gboolean proto_tree_print(print_dissections_e print_dissections,
                                         epan_dissect_t *edt,
                                         GHashTable *output_only_tables,
                                         print_stream_t *stream);
-WS_DLL_PUBLIC gboolean print_hex_data(print_stream_t *stream, epan_dissect_t *edt);
+
+/*
+ * Hexdump options for ASCII:
+ */
+
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_MASK            (0x0003U)
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_OPTION(option)  ((option) & HEXDUMP_ASCII_MASK)
+
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_INCLUDE         (0x0000U) /* include ASCII section no delimiters (legacy tshark behavior) */
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_DELIMIT         (0x0001U) /* include ASCII section with delimiters, useful for reliable detection of last hexdata */
+#define HEXDUMP_ASCII_EXCLUDE         (0x0002U) /* exclude ASCII section from hexdump reports, if we really don't want or need it */
+
+/*
+ * Hexdump option for displaying data sources:
+ */
+
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_MASK           (0x0004U)
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_OPTION(option) ((option) & HEXDUMP_SOURCE_MASK)
+
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_MULTI          (0x0000U) /* create hexdumps for all data sources assigned to a frame (legacy tshark behavor) */
+#define HEXDUMP_SOURCE_PRIMARY        (0x0004U) /* create hexdumps for only the frame data */
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC gboolean print_hex_data(print_stream_t *stream, epan_dissect_t *edt, guint hexdump_options);
 
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC void write_pdml_preamble(FILE *fh, const gchar* filename);
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC void write_pdml_proto_tree(output_fields_t* fields, gchar **protocolfilter, pf_flags protocolfilter_flags, epan_dissect_t *edt, column_info *cinfo, FILE *fh, gboolean use_color);
